highlights: 63 new confirmed cases (Ituri 46, Nord-Kivu 12, Haut-Uele 5) and 34 new deaths (Ituri 26, Nord-Kivu 6, Haut-Uele 2) take the DRC cumulative cleanly to 2536 confirmed / 1033 deaths (CFR 40.7%) with no harmonization this cycle (2473 + 63; 999 + 34). New confirmations rose 50 -> 63 while deaths rose only 32 -> 34, so the day's death-to-case ratio fell to 0.54 from 0.64. Deaths and confirmations of the same day are not the same cohort, so this is a reporting-ratio movement and NOT a case-fatality estimate; the cumulative CFR moved 40.4% -> 40.7%. Laboratory positives (46 + 12 + 5 = 63) equal the day's confirmations exactly, now across three reporting provinces. Tableau 1 prints a Total of 2531 that disagrees with its own province rows (which sum to 2536) and with Tableau 2 and the headline; 2536 is promoted.

NO new affected health zone was reported. The roster holds at 47 touched, 46 actively transmitting, and every cumulative zone delta equals that zone's printed day column, so nothing was silently restated. Ituri's new cases concentrate at Bunia (24), Rwampara (9), with Drodro and Fataki at 3 each; Ituri holds 88.6% of cumulative cases and 73.0% of the day's confirmations. Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) reaches 55 days without a confirmed case.

National contact follow-up fell to 77.2% (10765/13936) from 82.0%, and this cycle the fall is a GENUINE deterioration in the epicentre rather than a composition effect: Ituri dropped 81.8% -> 75.4% while Nord-Kivu held flat (81.9% -> 81.7%) and the reporting composition was unchanged from last cycle. The source itself flags the Ituri decline for investigation. The same epicentre pattern runs through alert investigation, where the national rate stayed high at 87.4% while Ituri fell again, 72.8% -> 66.7%, leaving 166 alerts uninvestigated; the national figure is carried by Nord-Kivu's 98.8% (902/913) on a much larger volume.

17 of the day's 34 confirmed deaths were community deaths detected by post-mortem swab (50.0%; Ituri 10 of 26, 38.5%), against 17 in-CTE deaths. A community-death share at half of all confirmed deaths is a surveillance-reach signal: those chains were not under care when the patient died, and it is coherent with the falling alert-investigation and contact-follow-up performance in the same province. 306 suspect cases were validated on the day (218 living, 88 community deaths).

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 20/07): 1415 alerts of the day (1399 new + 16 Report-J-1) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Tshopo; Haut-Uele and Sud-Kivu are ND on every alert row this cycle and are excluded from the denominators rather than counted as zero. Province rows sum exactly on every column (498+913+4 = 1415 reported; 332+902+3 = 1237 investigated; 160+55+3 = 218 living; 55+33+0 = 88 community deaths; 215+88+3 = 306 suspects, and 218 + 88 = 306). The national investigation rate 1237/1415 = 87.4% as printed, but it is volume-weighted toward Nord-Kivu (902/913 = 98.8%) and MASKS the epicentre: Ituri fell 72.8% -> 66.7% (332/498), leaving 166 alerts uninvestigated, a third consecutive cycle of decline (86.4% -> 75.6% -> 72.8% -> 66.7%).

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge, activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure the teams and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of responders (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; resumption announced after the intervention of Ituri's military governor) interrupts response activities including safe and dignified burials.
challenges.response: Regularise responder payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy 129.1% in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 78.5% in Ituri (556 patients for 708 beds), raising admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance remains weak: Ituri 75.4%, Nord-Kivu 81.7%, both far below the 95% operational target, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted; the source asks specifically to investigate the fall observed in Ituri.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision; investigate the Ituri decline.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points cause transfer and isolation delays.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, 15%) drive high nosocomial infection risk, with 121 first-line personnel infected and 36 dead.
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) and high mobility raise the risk of urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Installation of proximity laboratories (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo) is incomplete, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilisation and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services is compromised, raising indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of essential-service continuity.

priorities.priority: Reverse the alert-investigation fall in the epicentre (Ituri 66.7%, 166 alerts uninvestigated, a third consecutive cycle of decline) rather than reading the volume-weighted national 87.4%, and restore Haut-Uele alert reporting, ND on every alert row this cycle.

Investigate and reverse the genuine Ituri contact-follow-up decline (81.8% -> 75.4%), which the source itself flags; the national move to 77.2% is Ituri's drop, not a composition effect, with Nord-Kivu flat at 81.7% and both far below the 95% target.

Relieve Nord-Kivu isolation saturation at 129.1% (182 of 141 beds), the one genuine capacity emergency on this surface, and restore ND bed reporting in Haut-Uele and Tshopo. Ituri needs no capacity investigation: its 78.5% is on trend (708 beds) and its bed row now reads 709 -> 708, confirming SitRep66's 798 was a one-cycle data-entry outlier.

Address the community-death share (17 of 34 confirmed deaths, 50.0%; Ituri 10 of 26 at 38.5%) with active case-finding and safe-burial coverage; deaths detected only at post-mortem swab mark chains that were never under care, coherent with the falling alert and contact performance in the same province.

Sustain the newly online Haut-Uele diagnostic block and complete decentralised capacity (Logo installed; Butembo and Mambasa outstanding); read positivity movements as testing-volume, not prevalence, since day positives again equal the day's confirmations.
Sustain residual surveillance in Sud-Kivu, where Miti-Murhesa reaches 55 days without a confirmed case and contact follow-up is closed, toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration.

Ituri bed capacity is flat (709 -> 708) and SitRep66's 798 is now confirmed as a one-cycle outlier by two consecutive on-trend cycles. Ituri bed capacity across SitRep62-68 reads 693, 693, 700, 706, 798, 709, 708 with occupancy 79.2%, 78.1%, 78.3%, 76.3%, 69.3%, 78.4%, 78.5%. SitRep68's 708 is essentially the value SitRep66's 798 spike should have printed: 708 differs from 798 by one digit in the tens place, makes the capacity series monotonic, and prints occupancy on the same ~78% plateau as every neighbouring cycle. The most economical reading remains a data-entry slip in SitRep66 that propagated to its bed count, its derived 69.3% occupancy and the national 939 (= 798 + 141, which would have been 849). SitRep66's printed values are preserved as published and never silently corrected. Consequence for readers: there is NO capacity change to report in Ituri this cycle, and the earlier apparent 'occupancy jump' at SitRep67 must not be re-narrated as pressure. National capacity is flat (850 -> 849 beds). Nord-Kivu's 129.1% (182/141), up marginally from 128.4% (181/141), remains genuine saturation.

National contact follow-up 77.2% (10765/13936) is a GENUINE decline from SitRep67's 82.0%, driven by the epicentre and NOT by composition. Ituri fell 81.8% -> 75.4% while Nord-Kivu held flat (81.9% -> 81.7%), Tshopo stayed at 100.0% (75/75), and the reporting composition (Haut-Uele ND, Sud-Kivu closed) was unchanged from last cycle. This is the 'chute observee en Ituri' the source's own challenge table asks to investigate; last cycle that fall had not yet occurred, this cycle it has. It must be read as deteriorating epicentre performance, the opposite of last cycle's composition-driven 'improvement'.

Ituri fell 72.8% -> 66.7% (332/498) with 166 alerts uninvestigated, a third consecutive cycle of decline (86.4% -> 75.6% -> 72.8% -> 66.7%), while the national figure is carried by Nord-Kivu's 902/913 = 98.8% on a much larger alert volume.
